metaDescription: Stop Cell C data disappearing by checking app usage, hotspot, bundle expiry, and fallback settings so your balance lasts longer between top-ups today.
h1: How to stop data disappearing Cell C
quickAnswer: First separate Cell C bundle consumption, expiry or restricted allowances from airtime or account charges after data runs out. Save a balance reading and compare it with phone app usage for the same SIM and dates. Change the setting supported by those records, then check again. Out-of-bundle controls limit extra spending; they do not stop apps using an active bundle.

causes.cause: Apps or a shared connection consumed the allowance
causes.explanation: Downloads, streaming, syncing and hotspot clients can use mobile data. Check the app report for the relevant period before identifying a cause.

causes.cause: A bundle expired or its remaining wallet is restricted
causes.explanation: Record the purchase's expiry and whether the remaining allowance is anytime, night or service-specific. Expired or restricted data is different from ordinary app consumption.

causes.cause: Extra spending continued after usable data ended
causes.explanation: Compare airtime and billed charges separately from the data balance. Out-of-bundle consent and spend limits concern this extra spending, rather than the amount of data an app consumes.

causes.cause: The counters cover different periods or SIMs
causes.explanation: A phone usage report and an operator balance are different records. Align the dates and mobile-data SIM; a difference alone does not prove a billing fault.

cellc: Save the current Cell C app or self-service data balance, airtime balance, bundle name and expiry. Note each allowance category separately. Cell C's public guidance says balances can also be tracked through USSD; follow the current menu for your SIM.

Compare phone usage over the same dates and for the same SIM. On Google Pixel: Settings > Network & internet > SIMs > App data usage. Other Android menu names vary by manufacturer. On iPhone: Settings > Cellular or Mobile Data, then scroll to app usage; the current-period counter may cover different dates from your bundle.

Restrict the app you identified, rather than guessing from the balance alone. On iPhone, turn off mobile data for that app to leave Wi-Fi access. On Android, check the handset's background-data controls. Pause mobile downloads and backups and turn off an unused hotspot; restrictions can delay syncing or notifications.

For extra spending, open Cell C Spend Control in the app, self-service website or *147#. Choose no opt-in or R0 for out-of-bundle data if you want data access to stop when your included allowance is depleted. Save the confirmation; do not choose unlimited access by mistake.

Read the effective date of a Spend Control change. Cell C says a lower limit can apply only from the next month if spending already exceeds it, and past out-of-bundle charges are not refunded by changing the limit. Turn mobile data off while an uncertain change is being confirmed.

Check the exact bundle terms before extending or buying more data. Cell C's general rollover page and its data FAQ give different rollover descriptions; do not assume all products roll over. Keep the original purchase and expiry evidence.

After a short controlled period, compare another timestamped balance with phone usage. If the change remains unexplained, use Cell C support with both readings. Its data FAQ lists 135 and the official self-service route; request a reference and an explanation of the affected allowance or charge.

preventionTips: Check both expiry and remaining usable allowance before relying on a balance.
Use Wi-Fi for large downloads and backups and turn off an unused hotspot.
Use handset usage warnings where supported, with reporting dates matched to your bundle.
Check out-of-bundle and recurring-purchase settings separately; neither explains every reduction in a data balance.

faqs.question: Why does my Cell C data drop overnight?
faqs.answer: Check downloads, backups, app activity and hotspot clients for the same hours, and check the bundle expiry. A lower balance in the morning alone does not establish which cause applies or prove an operator error.

faqs.question: Does out-of-bundle control stop my Cell C bundle running out?
faqs.answer: No. It controls extra spending after the usable allowance ends. Apps can still consume an active bundle. Use phone usage reports to identify consumption and airtime or account records to investigate additional charges.

faqs.question: How do I stop out-of-bundle data spending on Cell C?
faqs.answer: Use Cell C Spend Control through the app, self-service website or *147# and select no opt-in or R0 for out-of-bundle data. Save the confirmation and effective date. A lower limit may apply next month if you already spent more; changing it does not refund earlier charges.

faqs.question: Can I extend unused Cell C data?
faqs.answer: It depends on the product. Cell C's general data guidelines and data FAQ publish different rollover descriptions. Check your bundle's own terms and purchase confirmation instead of assuming another purchase extends every allowance. Ask support to resolve an unclear expiry before paying for an extension.

faqs.question: Why does my phone show different usage from the operator?
faqs.answer: The phone measures its own traffic and may use a different reporting period or SIM. Align the dates and save the report before resetting counters. Use it to identify likely app activity; ask the operator to explain a disputed account balance.

uniqueValueSummary: Use three records together: your Cell C allowance and expiry, phone app usage for matching dates, and airtime or billed charges. The sequence below helps choose between an app restriction, an expiry enquiry and an out-of-bundle spending control. Make one supported change, save its confirmation and compare a later balance. If the evidence still does not explain the change, take those records to support instead of treating another top-up as a fix.
officialSupportContext: Cell C's Spend Control guidance lists its app, self-service website and *147#. R0/no opt-in stops out-of-bundle data access after included data is depleted; it does not protect an active bundle from app use. Its data FAQ lists 135 for support. Public rollover descriptions differ, so use the specific bundle terms and ask Cell C to confirm unresolved expiry or rollover questions. DataCost cannot access your private account, change limits or reverse deductions.
evidenceToCollect: Two timestamped Cell C balance readings for the same SIM, with each data wallet and airtime or billed amount shown separately.

whenThisDoesNotApply: This workflow is for diagnosing mobile-phone usage, expiry and additional spending.
